quiz.q: Which Database operations implement POST, PATCH and GET in the Employee API?
quiz.explain: POST inserts the employee, PATCH updates it, GET selects it by employee ID.

quiz.q: Where does the class put the actual processing for each operation?
options: Directly in the scaffolded resource flow
In a private flow in an implementation XML, called from the scaffolded flow via Flow Reference
quiz.explain: Scaffolded flows stay thin and use a Flow Reference; after processing, control returns to the main flow and the Listener responds.

quiz.q: You moved the Listener and APIkit router configs into global-config.xml. Does the Listener still find its configuration?
options: No — configs must stay in the same file as the flow
Yes — global elements are available to the whole project wherever they are
Only if global-config.xml is in src/main/resources
quiz.explain: Global elements are project-wide; best practice is to keep all of them in one XML.

quiz.q: After moving global elements, Studio still shows "name must be unique", even after saving and refreshing. What fixed it in class?
quiz.explain: It was a Studio display glitch; closing and reopening the project cleared it.

quiz.q: You move a scaffolded resource flow into another XML file in the project. What happens to routing?
options: It breaks — flows must be in the router's XML
It still works — the router routes by flow name, not file location
quiz.explain: The router uses the generated flow name; the flow can live in any XML of the project.

quiz.q: Why did the instructor delete the APIkit console flow?
options: It's a web UI for testing generated from the RAML, and testing is done with Postman
quiz.explain: The APIkit console isn't needed when you test with Postman.

quiz.q: Where should loggers go around a Database Insert, according to best practice?
options: Only at the end of the flow
Before and after the external call, plus start and end loggers for the flow
Loggers aren't needed for DB calls
quiz.explain: A DB call leaves the Mule app (external call). Loggers before and after show from logs exactly where processing stopped.

quiz.q: You copy post-employee.xml to create patch-employee.xml and Studio says "Flow name should be unique". What's the fix?
options: Rename the copied flow — flow names must be unique in the project
quiz.explain: The copy kept the same flow name. Rename each flow and also fill in the operation-specific SQL.

quiz.q: A Database operation shows "Required element SQL query text is missing". What's the cause?
options: The SQL query hasn't been written in the operation yet
The connector config has a default name
quiz.explain: Copy-paste builds structure, but each operation still needs its own SQL.

quiz.q: Which JDBC driver option did the class use for the MySQL connection?
quiz.explain: All three options exist; the class used Add recommended libraries. The driver establishes the connection between Mule and the DB.

quiz.q: While scrolling, the Secure Properties algorithm drop-down changed from AES/CBC. What's the risk?
options: Decryption fails because algorithm and mode must match what was used to encrypt
quiz.explain: Keep AES/CBC unchanged; it must match the encryption settings.

quiz.q: A student's OAuth token returns 400 / invalid token. Which is one of the checks suggested?
options: Check whether it is sent exactly as specified — e.g. a missing or extra Bearer word
quiz.explain: Also check the generation parameters, whether it expired, and whether it's a one-time token.

cards.back: POST → **Insert**, PATCH → **Update**, GET → **Select**.

cards.front: How do you structure a Mule project's code?
cards.back: Thin scaffolded flows → Flow Reference → implementation flows in separate XMLs; global elements in `global-config`; shared error handler in `common`; properties in `src/main/resources`.
A private flow with the actual processing, called via Flow Reference from the scaffolded flow.
One XML (e.g. `global-config`) holding all global elements, kept in the `common` folder.

cards.front: Studio shows stale errors after moving configs
cards.back: Close and reopen the project. (Package Explorer showed files properly when Project Explorer didn't.)
Copy a tested error-handler XML from a previous project into `common`, adapt the payload structure, and remove the generated handler.
A web-based UI to test APIs, generated from the RAML. Deleted when testing with Postman.

cards.front: Must resource flows stay in the router's XML?
cards.back: No — the router routes by flow name; flows can be in any XML.
Use **kebab-case**, e.g. `post-employee-implementation-flow`; names must be unique in the project.
Rename them, e.g. "Flow reference to post employee", so you can see where they go without clicking.
A call leaving the Mule app (DB, HTTP…). Put a logger **before and after** it.

cards.front: Why loggers before and after external calls?
cards.back: Logs show whether the call started and completed — i.e. where a failure occurred.
90–95% of the time only 4–5: select, insert, update, delete…
So anyone can tell which system is used; defaults like `Database_Config_1` confuse people.
Use keys like `${database.host}`; sensitive ones via `${secure::database.username}` / `${secure::database.password}`.
Library that connects Mule to the DB. Options: local file, Maven dependency, **Add recommended libraries**.

cards.front: Who provides DB details in real projects?
cards.back: The **database team** creates DB/tables and sends host, port, DB name, username, password.
UIs for MySQL / Oracle — write select, insert, update, delete, create table.
Windows services manager: start/stop/restart the MySQL service and set its startup type.

cards.front: Can configs be shared across apps on CloudHub?
cards.back: No. Domain projects are on-prem only; CloudHub/RTF workers are isolated containers.
Check generation params, how it's sent (header, `Bearer`), expiry, and whether it's one-time use.
